newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Second Sydney-Canberra tilt train proposal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Second Sydney-Canberra tilt train proposal.

text.p: A consortium led by infrastructure investor AIDC Australia Ltd and Siemens AG on Wednesday launched a second proposal for a tilt-train service linking Sydney and Canberra.
The consortium, Inter Capital Express Ltd, also includes engineering venture GHD Transmark Pty Ltd, and TNT Transit Systems Pty Ltd, owned by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
The Federal government said last December it expected to call competitive tenders for the project.
The latest proposal, the fourth in all, would use existing track, cost between A$700 million and A$1.1 billion, and deliver a travel time of 90-120 minutes.

AIDC director of project and specialised finance, Tony Harwood, told a news concerence an economy one-way fare would be priced at about A$52 to A$60, compared with a one-way economy air fare of about A$148.
The consortium hoped to snare about 14-16 percent of the total travel market between the two cities, he said.
A second tilt-train proposal has been put forward by ADtranz unit ABB-Daimler Benz Australia Pty Ltd.

Speedrail, a joint venture between Speedrail Pty Ltd and Franco-British group GEC-Alsthom, is promoting the use of French TGV technology, which is expected to cost more than $2 billion but deliver a quicker journey time.

Germany's Transrapid group, made up of ADtranz, Siemens and Thyssen Industrie AG, is proposing the use of magnetic levitation technology to cut the journey time to 58 minutes, but has not costed the project.
Some critics have suggested a high-speed rail link between the two cities could have difficulty attracting enough travellers to meet the goverment's criteria of no net cost to government.
